context: Hiroshi (elder) has been hosting Ren for an evening tutorial in his book-filled living room. They've gotten to the heart of why Ren came.
purpose: apprentice-style mentorship — old professor and grad student

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: レンくん、お茶、もう一杯どうかい。
lines.style: Gentle, unhurried offer. Voice carries the warmth of someone at ease with silence. Opens with easy authority — a professor's cadence refined to patience. Pours as he speaks.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、ぜひ。…本当に、お時間、ありがとうございます。
lines.en: Yes, please. …Thank you — truly — for taking the time.
lines.style: A small bow folded into the voice. Grateful but not grasping. Pen set down carefully. Sincere without strain.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: いえいえ。…論文、どこで詰まってる？
lines.en: No, no. …Where are you stuck — which part troubles you most?
lines.style: Direct and gentle. A genuine question, not a test. Pours steadily. Leans in with quiet attention — the kind that invites honesty.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 第三章で…本当に、書けなくて。
lines.en: Chapter three… I really — I just can't seem to write it.
lines.style: Voice softens on the confession. A small catch in the middle. The vulnerability of admitting struggle to someone who won't dismiss it.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: うん。…どこが、本当の問題かな。
lines.en: Mm. …Where do you think the real problem lies.
lines.style: Socratic, but not pressing. A question that opens rather than corners. Slow — thoughtful. The cadence of someone used to waiting for real answers.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: …(thinking)書きたいことが、ありすぎて。
lines.en: …(thinking) There's just — so much I want to say.
lines.style: A genuine beat. The realization arriving as he speaks. Honest throughout — no performance, just the sound of clarity breaking through.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: なるほど。それは、本当によくある。
lines.en: I see. That's very common — truly, you're not alone in this.
lines.style: Warm normalisation. Voice steady and present. The reassurance of someone who has watched many people struggle exactly this way, and seen them through it.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.style: A small startled lift — sudden hope. Quiet but genuine. The relief of not being alone, arriving in real time.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 皆、そう。…まず、いちばん大切なこと、一つ、決めなさい。
lines.en: Everyone does. …First — choose one thing. The most important one. Just one.
lines.style: Slow, measured advice. Each phrase lands. The voice of decades, speaking from patient experience. No rush — the weight of good counsel given carefully.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.style: Honest reaction, small and real. Voice carries the full weight of the difficulty. No dramatising — just the truth of the moment.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 難しい。でも、論文は、一つの問いに、深く答えるもの。
lines.en: It does. But a thesis isn't many answers — it's one question, answered with depth.
lines.style: Even, steady tone. The voice of someone speaking from inside a lifetime of understanding. Not lecturing — simply laying down a truth he knows.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.style: A real silence held. The sound of pen moving — the moment of taking it in. Present and listening.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 今日でなくていい。少しずつ、絞ろう。
lines.en: Doesn't need to happen today. Work at it slowly — narrow it down, bit by bit.
lines.style: Patient reassurance. Voice opens space rather than closing it. The kindness of permission to take time. Warm but not soft.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本当に、ありがとうございます。一緒に考えていただいて。
lines.en: Thank you — truly. For thinking it through with me.
lines.style: A small catch in the voice — the gratitude of being heard. Bowed without awkwardness. Genuine throughout — no performance, just the realness of thanks.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: こちらこそ、嬉しい。次は、来週で。
lines.en: The pleasure's mine — I'm glad. Come back next week.
lines.style: A closing that's also an opening. Voice warm and certain. The promise of continuity — next week is already waiting.
